subject: Hosted API sudden TPS suppression after kernel/quant change — FastCart escalation
messages:
From: Eli Sharp <eli@fastcart.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@fastcart.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa@fastcart.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API degradation impacting checkout traffic (p95/p99 + big TPS drop)

Kimberly —

We started seeing a major performance regression this morning around 07:50 PDT after your team’s maintenance window. Checkout flows that call the hosted /generate endpoint are timing out for some customers; our metrics show a p95 jump from ~110ms to ~480ms and p99s >1.2s. Token-per-second throughput for our standard batch (seq_length=512) dropped from ~4600 toks/sec to ~1100 toks/sec. Error rate also spiked briefly (5xxs).

We have a major seasonal traffic spike and this is blocking a ~6pm PST promotion. Please advise immediate mitigation steps and whether we can flip back any recent change you rolled minutes before.

Attaching a screenshot from our observability and will send logs in a follow-up.

—Eli
Eli Sharp
VP Engineering, FastCart
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Sharp <eli@fastcart.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, support@fastcart.ai
Date: 2028-09-14T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API degradation impacting checkout traffic (p95/p99 + big TPS drop)

Eli — thanks for flagging this, and apologies for the disruption. I’m escalating to infra and perf immediately (copied).

Immediate ask: can you confirm a span of a single failing request (request id or timestamp) and whether you saw any 5xx bodies? We’ll pull our traces and determine if this is a routing/quant/kernel selector regression or downstream infrastructure.

We’re planning a quick triage call in 15 min. I’ll propose a rollback if the change looks correlated.

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API degradation — initial triage notes

Folks — quick notes from the infra side after looking at rollout history:
- At 07:45 PDT we pushed an automated kernel-selector tweak (selector v2.3.7) that widened candidate kernels for some int8 quantized variants and changed the fallback priority. Rollout targeted hosted-api pool alpha (small percentage) but ramp logic may have misclassified a subset of customer routes.
- Telemetry shows a sudden increase in context-switch stalls and lower sustained token throughput on A100-type nodes serving FastCart’s region.
- No network-level failure or host OOMs in the timeframe.

I’m attaching the kernel diff and a proposed rollback plan (rollback to selector v2.3.6) that’s safe for hosted and can be staged by region. Suggest an immediate hold and staged rollback for affected nodes.

—Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: kernel-selector-diff.patch, rollback-plan.md
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API degradation — perf analysis (p95/p99 + tps)

Team — perf summary after running targeted benchmarking against the commit:
- Baseline (selector v2.3.6, quant profile q4_8): median latency 68ms, p95 112ms, p99 220ms, tokens/sec ~4600 (seq512).
- After selector v2.3.7 (expanded kernel choices + new scheduling heuristic): median 120ms, p95 452ms, p99 1.18s, tokens/sec ~1100.
- Regression appears concentrated when the runtime picks a new fused attention kernel on long sequences (>=384) under moderate concurrency; that kernel is much less friendly to int8 KV cache memory layout and causes increased memcpy stalls.
- Workaround options: force stable kernel set (force-selector to v2.3.6), pin quant profile to q4_8 with legacy kernel bindings, or temporarily increase instance burst capacity to mask throughput loss (costly).

Recommendation: immediate rollback of selector to v2.3.6 for the FastCart tenant’s serving pool + incremental canary to verify. I can run the bench and validate post-rollback within 12 minutes.

—Rishi
Perf Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Sharp <eli@fastcart.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@fastcart.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, support@fastcart.ai
Date: 2028-09-14T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API degradation impacting checkout traffic (p95/p99 + big TPS drop)

Eli / Marissa — thank you for the detail. We’ve identified a likely cause: an automated kernel-selector change (v2.3.7) correlated with your spike. Rishi’s bench shows the exact p95/p99 and TPS regressions you observed.

Planned mitigation (can start immediately upon your approval):
- Rollback kernel-selector to v2.3.6 for FastCart’s serving pool (target start: 09:30 PDT). Expected effect: restore previous kernel bindings and TPS to ~4.5k toks/sec within ~4–8 minutes of rollout windows.
- If rollback is insufficient, we will pin quant profile to q4_8 for your routes and perform a controlled warm restart (additional 12–20 min).
- As a precaution we’ll raise instance burst by one node group for the next 2 hours (to keep tail stable) while rollback completes.

We’ll log an SLA exception credit for the impacted window; I’ll bring this to revenue ops after we stabilize. Please reply with a quick approval to proceed.

Thanks,
Kimberly
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Executive Leadership <execs@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Exec note: FastCart outage risk + proposed hotfix and credits

Executive summary for context: FastCart saw a major p95/p99 regression and ~75% drop in tokens/sec after selector v2.3.7 rolled. Customer is on a revenue-producing seasonal campaign; risk of churn if not resolved quickly.

Proposed actions that need rapid sign-off:
- Approve immediate rollback of selector to v2.3.6 (low-risk) and allowance to perform a tenant-scoped rollback without full org-wide freeze.
- Approve up to $Xk in burst capacity costs for the emergency window.
- Approve a one-time SLA credit (we recommend 15% service credit for impacted 2-hr window) and a joint post-incident review with FastCart.

I’m standing by for sign-off; engineering is ready to action.

—Vivek
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Eli Sharp <eli@fastcart.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@fastcart.ai>, support@fastcart.ai
Date: 2028-09-14T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API degradation impacting checkout traffic (p95/p99 + big TPS drop)

Thanks — we authorise the rollback now. Please proceed and keep us posted on progress. We also want a short postmortem that explains why the canary/policy allowed this ramp to affect our tenant.

Appreciate the quick response.

—Eli
